_note: Government General Hospital, Vijayawada. Facts in English - the model answers in whatever language the patient used. Keywords carry BOTH scripts so search works either way. VERIFY against the real hospital before any public demo.

schemes.who_te: Any patient seeking outpatient consultation. No appointment needed for general OPD.
schemes.benefit_te: OPD runs Monday to Saturday, 8 in the morning to 1 in the afternoon. Registration closes at 12:30. Sunday is emergency only.
schemes.how_te: Come before 11 in the morning to avoid the long queue. Collect a token at the registration counter near the main entrance.

schemes.who_te: Every OPD patient gets a token at registration.
schemes.benefit_te: Tokens look like A-47 or B-112. The letter is your department block, the number is your turn. Announcements are made on the speaker in the waiting hall.
schemes.how_te: Keep the token slip in your hand. If you cannot hear the announcement, show your slip at the help desk and they will check your turn.

schemes.who_te: Patients looking for a specific department.
schemes.benefit_te: Ground floor Block A has Orthopaedics and Casualty. First floor Block A has General Medicine. Second floor Block C has the Laboratory and Pharmacy. Cardiology is on the first floor of Block B.
schemes.how_te: From the main gate, Block A is straight ahead. Block B is to the right past the canteen. Block C is behind Block A. Ask any staff member in a blue coat.

schemes.benefit_te: Bring your Aadhaar card, any old prescriptions and reports, and your Ayushman Bharat card if you have one. A referral slip is needed to see a specialist.
schemes.how_te: Keep everything in one folder. Without Aadhaar, registration takes much longer.

schemes.who_te: Anyone facing a medical emergency, day or night.
schemes.benefit_te: Call one zero eight for a free ambulance, any time of day or night. Casualty is open twenty four hours on the ground floor of Block A, to the left of the main gate.
schemes.how_te: Do not wait in the OPD queue for an emergency. Go straight to Casualty. Tell the guard at the gate it is an emergency and he will let you through.

schemes.who_te: Families listed under Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY.
schemes.benefit_te: Cashless treatment up to five lakh rupees per family per year. You pay nothing for covered procedures.
schemes.how_te: Bring your Ayushman card and Aadhaar to the Ayushman help desk near the registration counter. They will verify and open your case.

schemes.who_te: Patients who want to see a specialist rather than general OPD.
schemes.benefit_te: General OPD needs no appointment, just a token. Specialists need a referral from the general OPD doctor first.
schemes.how_te: Go to general OPD, get the referral, then book at the specialist counter on the first floor. Booking closes at noon.

schemes.who_te: Patients with a prescription from a hospital doctor.
schemes.benefit_te: Most medicines on the essential list are free at the hospital pharmacy. It is on the second floor of Block C, next to the laboratory.
schemes.how_te: Take your prescription to the pharmacy counter. Pharmacy is open 8 in the morning to 4 in the afternoon.

schemes.who_te: Patients with a test request from a doctor.
schemes.benefit_te: Blood and urine tests are free with a doctor's slip. Sample collection is 8 to 11 in the morning only. Most reports come the same evening.
schemes.how_te: Laboratory is on the second floor of Block C. Come fasting if the doctor asked for a sugar test.

schemes.who_te: Family members visiting an admitted patient.
schemes.benefit_te: Visiting hours are 11 to 12 in the morning and 5 to 7 in the evening. One attendant may stay overnight with the patient.
schemes.how_te: Collect a visitor pass from the security desk at the ward entrance. Children under ten are not allowed in the wards.
